Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Runner timing diagnostics

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Set a runner's profile_clock to a monotonic microsecond clock. profile_metrics records bounded histograms and optional profile_sample(user, metric, elapsed_us) receives raw durations. The sample callback should write to preallocated storage; it must not affect gameplay or block on I/O. Nothing is serialized or transmitted.

Metric Measured work
Advance An ordinary timeline advance: candidate copy, model execution and timeline validation/commit
Pump Complete network pump, including nested snapshot/replay work
Snapshot Server encoding/delta/send/cache work, or client validation/decompression/decoding/acknowledgment
Replay The authoritative correction and suffix replay operation
Snapshot_Encode Server frame/packet construction and canonical encoding, or client canonical decoding
Snapshot_Delta Server delta/envelope construction, or client envelope validation, reconstruction and target-hash verification
Snapshot_Hash Server digest of the newly encoded canonical snapshot
Snapshot_Cache Retaining the canonical snapshot and its already computed digest
Snapshot_Validate Client metadata, model-state and held-control validation
Snapshot_Send Server transport submission or client acknowledgement submission

Pump is inclusive; do not add its total to nested Snapshot/Replay totals. Advance excludes client bootstrap catch-up and replayed ticks (Replay measures the latter as a complete operation). Snapshot samples include rejected, duplicate and deferred attempts: that work still consumed time. Server stepping may flush snapshots outside the network pump. These are elapsed wall times, not thread CPU times.

Snapshot subphases are adjacent portions of the outer measurement. A rejected or deferred operation may finish before reaching a subphase boundary, so their sample counts need not equal the outer count. Clock failures increment timing errors; they do not alter packet decisions. Existing enum values remain stable; new subphase values are appended, and applications mapping metrics must handle them.

Client replay counters/histograms remain in Stats for compatibility. Optional profiling failures do not fail simulation. Native tests compare profiled/unprofiled worlds and protocol bytes and verify samples are delivered for the relevant phases.

Scrapyard's bench_start/bench_finish adds presentation and whole-frame samples, writes a bounded CSV only after measurement, and reports protocol bytes and timeline allocation sizes. Presentation measures command submission even in headless mode; it is not GPU render time. Its final report computes exact nearest-rank percentiles from raw samples rather than calling histogram bounds exact percentiles.

Large value copies should avoid unnecessary aggregate intermediates. In the Scrapyard specialization, independent assignments and pointer selection over local owned presentation copies preserve behavior while avoiding a pathological SLP compile. See the recorded IR/build evidence.
